widgets_values: One continuous take, 5 seconds, no cuts, keep the ukiyo-e woodblock look exactly: flat ochre sky, pale blue-green canopies, indigo skin, orange roses. The camera stays WIDE and creeps forward very gently, only a small push-in, always keeping the whole beast, its forest and the marsh in frame. 0-2s: the colossal forest rhinoceros shifts its weight and takes one heavy half-step forward - foreleg lifting clear of the water, setting down, a ring of ripples pushing through the lotus leaves - while the canopy on its back sways hard, pale leaves shake loose, and its tail flicks. 2-4s: the four tiny travellers walk a slow circuit around its forelegs and out in front of its lowered head, staves tapping the shallow water; the beast swings its head down toward them, ears turning, breath pluming slightly in the cool air. 4-5s: it takes one more half-step and stops; the water rings out and the travellers pause beneath its horn. Slow ceremonial motion, no shake, no zoom snap, no close-up. Sound: deep footfalls in shallow water, canopy creaking and rustling, a heavy exhale through the nostrils, soft staves on water, birds - no music, no voices.
